title: Download Daedalus from the official website

summary.text: Daedalus is a desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux, and its download site is daedaluswallet.io. Each installer has a matching .asc signature file, so you can check that the installer is genuine before you run it.

problem.text: A user needs to know where to download Daedalus safely and which Linux installation options exist.

symptoms.text: The user is unsure which download site is genuine.

daedalus.notes: Behavior read from the Daedalus 11.6.0 release notes and the 11.6.0 tag source. Check a newer release before relying on it for a later version.

causes.claim: The available evidence does not establish one cause.

resolutions.action: Open daedaluswallet.io/download and download the installer for your operating system with its .asc signature file.
resolutions.why: The download page is where Daedalus publishes each installer and its signature.

resolutions.action: On Linux, choose the Debian, RPM or Arch package, or the NixOS service in the flake, rather than the portable .bin installer, which is deprecated.
resolutions.why: The 11.6.0 release notes name these as the preferred Linux installation options.

resolutions.action: Before you run the installer, check its SHA256 checksum and its signature as the download page explains.
resolutions.why: A matching checksum and signature show that the installer was not altered.

expected_outcome.text: You have an installer from daedaluswallet.io whose SHA256 checksum and signature match, ready to run.

do_not: Do not run an installer whose SHA256 checksum or signature does not match.

evidence.rationale: Release notes, tagged source and portal pages directly state the behavior; this is source inspection, not runtime testing.

faq.reason: Common support topic with a short answer that every cited source supports.
